title: Letters to Ash
logline: A widowed calligrapher burns a letter to his wife every night, until the fire writes back.
look: Sumi ink on rice paper, strokes that draw themselves, ink bleeding into wet paper; black, bone white and ember orange only; rising embers.
narrator: male, elderly, moderate pitch, american accent
Quiet, grief-worn, intimate, close to the microphone
music: Solo cello and low drone, crackling fire; a single high bell when the embers write; the cello resolves at dawn.

shots.direction: EWS · locked · fade in — black; one brush stroke draws a horizon; ink bleeds into mountains
MS 50mm · slow push · cut — an old calligrapher kneels at a low desk beside a brazier, writing
ECU macro · locked · cut — the brush forms a character; ink blooms into the paper
CU 85mm · hold · cut — he folds the letter and lays it in the brazier; embers rise
WS 24mm · tilt up · match cut on embers — embers drift into the night and for a moment draw the outline of a woman, then scatter
MS 50mm · locked · jump cuts — he writes again, faster, letter after letter; the brazier roars
CU 85mm · hold · cut — his hand trembles; the brush runs dry
EWS 24mm · slow tilt · cut — the embers gather into a single brush stroke that writes one character across the sky
CU 85mm · push in · cut — he reads it; a tear; the brazier dims
MS 50mm · locked · cut — he lays down the brush, leaves the last letter unburned, and opens the shutter: dawn
WS 35mm · slow drift · cut — plum blossoms draw themselves along a branch in morning light
EWS · locked · fade out — the opening horizon again, now with a rising sun

narration.text: For a year, he wrote to her every night.
And every night, he sent the letter up in fire.
Until the night it did. One word.
She had only ever wanted him to rest.
